title: Postgres — Debug & Runbook

panels.title: Postgres logs — $service | $search
panels.description: All Postgres primary/replica log lines. Narrow with the Service and Search variables at the top.

targets.rawSql: SELECT timestamp, message, service, level FROM default.logs WHERE service LIKE '$service' AND message ILIKE '%${search}%' AND $__timeFilter(timestamp) ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 500

panels.title: CPU usage % by pod
panels.description: Percentage of each Postgres pod's CPU limit in use.

targets.expr: (100 * (sum by (pod) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{namespace="pfa",pod=~"postgres.*",container!="",container!="POD"}[5m]))) / (sum by (pod) (container_spec_cpu_quota{namespace="pfa",pod=~"postgres.*",container!="",container!="POD"} / container_spec_cpu_period{namespace="pfa",pod=~"postgres.*",container!="",container!="POD"}))) and on(pod) (max by (pod) (container_last_seen{namespace="pfa"} @ end()) > scalar(max(timestamp(container_last_seen{namespace="pfa"} @ end()))) - 120)

panels.title: Memory usage % by pod
panels.description: Percentage of each Postgres pod's memory limit held. Nearing 100% means an OOM kill is next.

targets.expr: (100 * (sum by (pod) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{namespace="pfa",pod=~"postgres.*",container!="",container!="POD"})) / (sum by (pod) (container_spec_memory_limit_bytes{namespace="pfa",pod=~"postgres.*",container!="",container!="POD"}))) and on(pod) (max by (pod) (container_last_seen{namespace="pfa"} @ end()) > scalar(max(timestamp(container_last_seen{namespace="pfa"} @ end()))) - 120)

options.content:
## Copy/paste runbook

Run from the repo root. `DB_USER`, `DB_NAME` and `DB_PASSWORD` come from `.env`.

```bash
export DB_USER=$(sed -n 's/^DB_USER=//p' .env)
export DB_NAME=$(sed -n 's/^DB_NAME=//p' .env)
export DB_PW=$(sed -n 's/^DB_PASSWORD=//p' .env)
export PRIMARY=postgres-primary-0
export REPLICA=$(kubectl -n pfa get pod -l app=postgres-replica -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')
PSQL="kubectl -n pfa exec $PRIMARY -- env PGPASSWORD=$DB_PW psql -U $DB_USER -d $DB_NAME"
```

### 1. Is it healthy?

```bash
kubectl -n pfa exec $PRIMARY -- pg_isready -U "$DB_USER"
$PSQL -c 'select version();'
$PSQL -c 'select pg_is_in_recovery();'        # false on primary
$PSQL -c '\dn'                                # auth, finance, groups, activity
kubectl -n pfa logs statefulset/postgres-primary --tail=100
```

### 2. Replication (why reads lag)

```bash
# primary
$PSQL -c "select client_addr, state, sync_state, sent_lsn, replay_lsn, replay_lag from pg_stat_replication;"
# replica
kubectl -n pfa exec $REPLICA -- env PGPASSWORD=$DB_PW psql -U $DB_USER -d $DB_NAME \
  -c "select status, sender_host, received_lsn, replay_lsn, last_msg_receipt_time from pg_stat_wal_receiver;"
kubectl -n pfa exec $REPLICA -- env PGPASSWORD=$DB_PW psql -U $DB_USER -d $DB_NAME \
  -c "select now() - pg_last_xact_replay_timestamp() as replay_lag;"
```

`replay_lag` above a second means the query-service read model is stale.
Repeated `could not connect to the primary server` in the replica logs means
the primary was down or the Service DNS/port changed.

### 3. Connections and locks

```bash
$PSQL -c "select state, count(*) from pg_stat_activity group by 1 order by 2 desc;"
$PSQL -c 'show max_connections;'
$PSQL -c "select pid, wait_event_type, wait_event, state, now()-query_start as age, left(query,100) from pg_stat_activity where state <> 'idle' order by age desc;"
$PSQL -c "select blocked.pid, blocking.pid as blocking_pid, left(blocked.query,60) as blocked_query, left(blocking.query,60) as blocking_query from pg_stat_activity blocked join pg_stat_activity blocking on blocking.pid = any(pg_blocking_pids(blocked.pid)) where cardinality(pg_blocking_pids(blocked.pid)) > 0;"
```

Cancel a runaway query with `select pg_cancel_backend(<pid>);`; use
`pg_terminate_backend(<pid>)` only when cancellation does not take.

### 4. Slow queries

```bash
$PSQL -c "select pid, now()-query_start as age, state, left(query,160) from pg_stat_activity where state = 'active' and now()-query_start > interval '30 seconds' order by age desc;"
$PSQL -c "select datname, xact_commit, xact_rollback, blks_read, blks_hit, round(100.0*blks_hit/nullif(blks_hit+blks_read,0),2) as cache_hit_pct from pg_stat_database;"
```

A falling cache hit ratio plus rising `blks_read` usually means a missing index
or a table scan over a table that outgrew memory.

### 5. Storage, bloat and vacuum

```bash
$PSQL -c "select datname, pg_size_pretty(pg_database_size(datname)) from pg_database order by pg_database_size(datname) desc;"
$PSQL -c "select schemaname||'.'||relname as table, pg_size_pretty(pg_total_relation_size(relid)) as total from pg_catalog.pg_statio_user_tables order by pg_total_relation_size(relid) desc limit 20;"
$PSQL -c "select relname, n_live_tup, n_dead_tup, last_autovacuum, last_autoanalyze from pg_stat_user_tables order by n_dead_tup desc limit 20;"
$PSQL -c "select relname, indexrelname, idx_scan from pg_stat_user_indexes order by idx_scan asc limit 20;"
kubectl -n pfa exec $PRIMARY -- df -h /var/lib/postgresql/data
```

High `n_dead_tup` needs a `VACUUM (ANALYZE) <table>;` (never inside a
transaction). Low `idx_scan` on an index means it is a write-only liability.

### 6. Outbox and background work

```bash
$PSQL -c "select status, count(*), min(created_at), max(created_at) from finance.outbox_events group by 1 order by 2 desc;"
$PSQL -c 'select * from pg_stat_bgwriter;'
```

Pending outbox rows that never drain mean the command-service publisher is
down or RabbitMQ is unreachable. Rising `checkpoints_req` means WAL pressure.

### 7. Last resort

```bash
kubectl -n pfa rollout restart statefulset/postgres-primary   # safe: PVC kept
kubectl -n pfa get pods -o wide                                # confirm both pods
```

Never delete the PVC. Do not promote the replica without checking
`START-STOP.md` first.

description: Postgres primary/replica logs, pod pressure, replication health and copy-paste psql commands. Start here when writes, reads or replica freshness look wrong.
